endingSlide.heading: Tag someone choosing between Seoul and Tokyo

caption:
Seoul is 15–25% cheaper overall. But for the right earner, Tokyo's tax structure changes everything.

For most remote workers ($50–100K/year): Seoul wins on budget, transport, healthcare, and cafe culture as free workspace. Unlimited transit for $41/month and nobody kicks you out after two hours.

For high earners ($100K+): Japan's Digital Nomad visa makes you a non-resident. Foreign income is taxed at 0%. Korea's 183-day rule triggers worldwide income tax at 6–45%. At $120K, that gap can be larger than the entire rent difference.

Neither city is universally cheaper. Neighborhood choice matters more than city choice. Gangnam vs Hongdae is a 40–60% rent swing inside Seoul alone.
